subject: Re: Post-demo — Model fit & benchmark links (PayFlow)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@payflow.com>, Tom Bennett <tom@payflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & next steps — model fit for PayFlow

Hi Samantha / Tom,

Great to meet you both this morning — thanks for walking through PayFlow's authorization pipeline and latency requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Goal we heard: decrease fraud false positives without adding >300ms p99 latency on authorization path at peak TPS (~150 TPS sustained bursts to 300 TPS).
- Suggested approach: run a small eval suite using your representative prompt set against two model tiers:
  1) rwd-3b-quant (cost-efficient, good for throughput-sensitive routes)
  2) rwd-13b-chat-8bit (higher quality for edge-case classification)

Attachments: payflow_prompt_set_v1.txt (example prompts + expected labels) and our Redwood-verified performance profiles (pdf) — contains TPS guidance and latency percentiles for each model and common instance types.

Next steps:
1) If you can confirm a sanitized sample of ~500 representative requests (anonymized), Marissa and I will run the eval and return a side-by-side quality + performance matrix.
2) We'll also include prompt tuning suggestions and an initial cost estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted routing.
3) Quick follow-up: propose Tue 6/16 11am PT for a 30-min results review. Please let me know if that works.

Thanks again — Alex

--
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — model fit for PayFlow

Thanks Alex — really useful recap. A couple quick clarifications before we send sample data: 

- Can you share the Redwood-verified performance pages you referenced (TPS guidance + latency percentiles) so we can validate headroom for our p99 < 300ms target?
- For the eval, how long does a turn-around usually take for ~500 examples? We have a compliance window for sharing even anonymized logs.

Also adding a hard requirement: in production some routes will run at sustained 150 TPS for minutes at a time. We need to understand warm vs cold start behavior and expected tail latency under sustained load.

If it's helpful we can also share a small subset of redacted logs first.

Samantha
Head of Fraud Ops | PayFlow Inc.
samantha@payflow.com | (212) 555-0134

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap & next steps — model fit for PayFlow (internal notes)

Alex — forwarding a quick internal note with model / perf links that will answer Samantha's questions. Copying below so you can paste into the customer reply.

Notes: 
- Perf pages: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/payflow-20260612 (public link for this eval) — contains per-model TPS curves, median/95/99 latencies on our hosted fleet and Dedicated GPU profiles (p50/p95/p99).
- Warm vs cold: our published numbers are for steady-state (warm) performance. Cold-starts are typically <2s for cold container spin-up on hosted with autoscale; Dedicated capacity avoids cold-starts with reserved workers. We'll include a warm-up ramp test in the eval to mirror sustained 150 TPS.
- Recommended runs: 500 examples with 3 passes (total 1,500 inference calls) to characterize variance; allow 24-36 hours for runs depending on queue and jobs; we can expedite to 6-12 hours if you opt for Dedicated burst or prioritize the job.
- Model recommendations: rwd-3b-quant (baseline), rwd-13b-chat-8bit (higher quality); optionally test a 70B quantized chat variant if you want to prioritize edge-case recall — note cost/latency trade-offs listed on the perf page.
- Prompt tweaks: add a 1-2 sentence explicit instruction at top of prompt to reduce hallucinations (see payflow_prompt_set_v1.txt, header examples).

Links to paste: 
- Redwood benchmark: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/payflow-20260612
- Performance profiles pdf (internal): https://drive.redwood.com/perf_profiles/redwood_performance_profiles.pdf
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8421

Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Samantha — thanks for the quick reply and the latency callout. See below for the links and a short plan that addresses warm/cold behavior and p99 headroom.

1) Benchmark & perf links (Redwood-verified):
   - Public eval dashboard: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/payflow-20260612
   - Performance profiles (pdf): attached (redwood_performance_profiles.pdf) — includes p50/p95/p99 at several TPS points and notes on instance types used for the runs.

2) Warm vs cold / sustained loads:
   - The dashboard numbers are steady-state (warm). We'll add a warm-up ramp during the run to mirror your 150 TPS sustained scenario and capture p99 under steady bursts.
   - If you'd like Dedicated reserved workers, that removes cold-start variance entirely — Marissa's note above includes Dedicated throughput & latency targets.

3) Turn-around & next steps:
   - If you send the sanitized 500 examples, we'll queue the eval. Standard turnaround: 24-36 hours. Expedited: 6-12 hours if you mark the job as priority (or if you choose Dedicated burst).
   - I'll put a 30-min slot on Tue 6/16 11am PT to review results — if that doesn't work for you, propose a time and we'll adjust.

Attached: payflow_prompt_set_v1.txt (example prompt set), redwood_performance_profiles.pdf
